meanings.note: Placed directly before an indefinite noun without ال- to mean 'the last' (آخر يوم 'the last day', آخر الساحة 'the far end of the courtyard').

examples.trans: The attic room is at the end of the floor.
Today is the last day of the week.

meanings.note: Invariant comparative/superlative of حلو ('sweet, lovely').

examples.trans: It has the loveliest view of the courtyard.
This is the nicest day of the week.

meanings.note: Numeral 'four'; short form أربع (arba') directly before a plural noun (أربع طاولات 'four tables').

examples.trans: Room four is arriving today.
Four tables and eight chairs in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أسابيع.

examples.trans: Next week I have time off.
We stayed at the guesthouse all week.

meanings.note: Subject pronoun 'I' for any speaker.

examples.trans: I am Nour, the new receptionist.
I am Salma from the kitchen.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بنقذ, بينقذ).

examples.trans: Quick thinking saved breakfast!
You saved my whole trip.

meanings.note: Before an indefinite noun أول means 'first' (أول يوم 'first day'); after a definite noun الأول / الأولى agrees in gender (الصفحة الأولى 'the first page'). Also used adverbially ('first').

examples.trans: Welcome on your first day of work!
Read the first page calmly.

meanings.note: Exclamation of mild surprise or realization ('oh!').

examples.trans: Oh! My glasses are on my head!
Oh, look at the beauty of this ceiling!

meanings.note: Everyday conditional word 'if' for real possibilities.

examples.text: رني الجرس إذا احتجتي أي شي.
examples.trans: Ring the bell if you need anything.

examples.text: إذا فتحنا الساحة الصبح، الجيران بيفرحوا.
examples.trans: If we open the courtyard in the morning, the neighbours will be delighted.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: The reception desk is beside the door.
Thank you for the warm welcome.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بستنى, بيستنى).

examples.trans: Wait a moment, I have an idea!
The suitcase is still waiting for its owner.

meanings.note: Everyday noun for a person's or place's name; takes possessive endings directly (اسمي my name, اسمك your name).

examples.trans: What is your kind name?
My name is written here in the notebook.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian form of الاثنين ('Monday', and with ال also 'both / the two').

examples.trans: I started work on Monday morning.
Monday's bus arrived at seven.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: جمع.

examples.trans: The family gathers every Friday at noon.
On Friday the street is quiet.

meanings.note: Invariant spoken Jordanian relative pronoun ('who, which, that') for any gender or number.

examples.trans: That is what I want.
The inn that keeps a stranger's bag safe.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بنكتب, بينكتب).

examples.trans: Your name will be written in the big ledger!
The address was written in clear handwriting.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: بواب.

examples.trans: The wooden door is open now.
Someone knocked on the door.

meanings.note: Everyday word for 'tomorrow' (بكرا الصبح 'tomorrow morning').

examples.text: بكرا الصبح رح نسبق المي الباردة!
examples.trans: Tomorrow morning we will beat the cold water!
We booked a quiet dinner — will you join us tomorrow?

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian possessive word ('belonging to'); agrees in gender: تبع (m.), تبعت (f.), تبعون (pl.).

examples.text: اليوم آخر يوم بأسبوع التجربة تبعك.
examples.trans: Today is the last day of your trial week.
My brother's piano teacher!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: تجارب.

examples.trans: The trial week went by fast.
It was a very sweet experience.

meanings.note: Used both before a noun ('under, beneath') and standalone ('downstairs').

examples.trans: Let us bring it downstairs into the light.
The wide desk is under the window.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian numeral 'three'; short form تلات (talaat) directly before a plural noun (تلات سنين 'three years').

examples.trans: Three years was a long time.
One, two, three!

meanings.note: Adverb 'exact, completely, perfectly'.

examples.trans: Its size fits you perfectly.
The street is completely empty at noon.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian numeral 'eight'; short form تمن (taman) before a plural noun (تمن غرف 'eight rooms').

examples.text: عندنا تمن غرف وتمن مفاتيح نحاس.
examples.trans: We have eight rooms and eight brass keys.
He arrives at eight in the evening.

meanings.note: Means 'grandfather' (جدي my grandfather) and in عن جد ('really / seriously') means 'earnestness'.

examples.trans: My grandfather's workshop was on this street.
Did you really finish all the work?

meanings.note: Used both before a noun ('inside the bag') and standalone ('inside').

examples.trans: Look inside the suitcase, Nour!
The water is flowing inside!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: حارات.

examples.trans: The shop is right here in our neighbourhood.
Old Amman neighbourhoods are peaceful.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أحبار.

examples.trans: We wrote the name in blue ink.
The ink pen is on the desk.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أحلام.

examples.text: هاد كان حلم حياتي من زمان.
examples.trans: That was my lifelong dream.
At last our dreams came true.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun.

examples.trans: Life is sweet with kind people.
Never in my life have I seen a prettier view.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: خبازين.

examples.trans: The baker opens the oven at five in the morning.
The bakers' market is near the overpass.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بخبر, بيخبر).

examples.trans: Wait till I tell the bakers' market!
We told the guests the breakfast time.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بخبز, بيخبز).

examples.text: اخبزي قطع زوايا كتير يا سلمى!
examples.trans: Bake plenty of corner pieces, Salma!

examples.text: قديش بيقدر فرنك يخبز كل صبح؟
examples.trans: How much can your oven bake every morning?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: دائمة, plural: دائمين).

examples.trans: She became the permanent reception manager at the guesthouse.
He wrote it in the ledger in permanent ink.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: دفاتر.

examples.trans: We wrote the name in the booking ledger.
I forgot my leather notebook on the table.

meanings.note: Used in دوام كامل ('full-time job') and دوام جزئي ('part-time').

examples.trans: She started a new full-time job.
Office hours are from eight to five.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: رائعة, plural: رائعين).

examples.trans: A wonderful choice with morning tea!
The weather in the courtyard today is splendid.

meanings.note: Invariant spoken Levantine future marker placed before a subjunctive verb (without ب-).

examples.text: ضيفة غرفة أربعة رح تقعد كل الأسبوع.
examples.trans: Room four's guest will stay all week.

examples.text: تاني يوم ما رح يكون ممل!
examples.trans: The second day is not going to be boring!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: رسايل.

examples.trans: An official letter arrived at noon.
We read the letter line by line.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: ساحات.

examples.trans: The courtyard has a big jasmine tree.
We sat drinking tea in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: ساعات.

examples.trans: What time is it right now, please?
We arrived an hour ago on the dot.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: سخانات.

examples.trans: We started the boiler before breakfast.
The boiler room is down in the basement.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أسواق.

examples.text: سوق وسط البلد مليان حركة الصبح.
examples.trans: The downtown market is bustling in the morning.
We bought fresh herbs from the market.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb for 'to see, look, check' (بشوف / شاف).

examples.trans: Look inside the suitcase, Nour!
I will see you tomorrow at breakfast.

meanings.note: Singulative شجرة ('a tree', feminine), collective شجر ('trees').

examples.trans: We placed the table under the old tree.
We hear the rustle of tree leaves in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Universal Jordanian/Levantine word (from Turkish çanta) for any handbag, backpack, or travel suitcase.

examples.trans: This blue suitcase is very heavy.
We set the suitcases beside the reception desk.

meanings.note: Everyday spoken Jordanian noun for 'the morning' (الصبح in the morning, كل صبح every morning).

examples.trans: I drink black coffee every morning.
The morning bread is still hot.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أضعاف.

examples.trans: Today we baked double the usual amount.
The courtyard holds twice this number.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بضل, بيضل).

examples.trans: Family is what remains.
My teacup stayed intact inside the suitcase!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: طاولات.

examples.trans: We set four tables in the courtyard.
Breakfast is ready on the table.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: عالقة, plural: عالقين).

examples.text: فتحتي بابنا العالق من أول يوم!
examples.trans: You opened our sticking door on day one!
The key was stuck in the lock.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: عقود.

examples.trans: The lease contract is protected by law.
He works at the municipal contracts office.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بعمل, بيعمل).

examples.text: اليوم رح نعمل بيض عالطريقة الفرنسية!
examples.trans: Today we will make French-style eggs!
What do we do now with the rain coming down?

meanings.note: Means 'about' (عن الزبدة), 'off / away from' (عن جبيني), and appears in عن جد ('really!') and عن إذنك ('excuse me').

examples.trans: I will carry the suitcase up for you.
I heard your voices about the butter!

meanings.note: Marks location ('at, by') and with pronoun suffixes expresses possession: عندي ('I have'), عندك ('you have'), عندنا ('we have').

examples.trans: A taxi just stopped at the door.
I have a reservation under the name Suad.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بعين, بيعين).

examples.text: إذا ما عينتها، رح أعينها بمطبخي!
examples.trans: If you do not hire her, I will hire her in my kitchen!
They hired a new reception manager.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: غرف.

examples.trans: We have eight comfortable rooms at the guesthouse.
Room four is ready and clean.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بفتح, بيفتح).

examples.trans: The corner shop opens at seven.
Oh, the door finally opened!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أفران.

examples.text: لفائف القرفة طلعت من الفرن هلا.
examples.trans: The cinnamon rolls just came out of the oven.
The bakery down the street bakes in the morning.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: Breakfast is from seven thirty to ten.
We prepared a warm breakfast for the guests.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بقدر, بيقدر).

examples.text: بنقدر نقدم زبدة مالحة مع المربى؟
examples.trans: Can we serve salted butter with jam?

examples.text: ليش ما قدرت تعطيه القطار بإيدك؟
examples.trans: Why could you not hand him the train yourself?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun.

examples.trans: The warm scent of cinnamon filled the kitchen.
We ate a cinnamon roll with tea.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بقبل, بيقبل).

examples.trans: Will you accept staying on as our reception manager?
She accepted the invitation gladly.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: كافيهات.

examples.trans: We opened a small café in the house courtyard.
The morning café serves all the neighbours.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: كاملة, plural: كاملين).

examples.trans: He hired her for a full-time job at the guesthouse.
They stayed with us a full week.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: كبيرة, plural: كبار).

examples.trans: We use this big paper ledger.
You know older brothers well!

meanings.note: Before an indefinite singular noun كل means 'every' (كل يوم 'every day'); before a definite noun it means 'all / the whole' (كل الأسبوع 'all week').

examples.trans: Tell me everything I need to know.
Everyone is happy in the courtyard today.

meanings.note: In questions كم + singular noun asks 'how many?'; in statements كم + singular noun means 'a few' (كم دقيقة 'a few minutes').

examples.trans: Give him a few minutes, Rami.

examples.text: كم لفة قرفة بيقدر فرنك يخبز؟
examples.trans: How many cinnamon rolls can your oven bake?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: كميات.

examples.trans: We need double the amount for tomorrow morning.
This quantity is enough for ten guests.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: كيكات.

examples.text: كيكة الليمون الصفرا طلعت من الفرن.
examples.trans: The yellow lemon cake came out of the oven.
We sliced the cake into six equal pieces.

meanings.note: Versatile Jordanian noun meaning a wrapped parcel (اللفة البيضا), a pastry roll (لفة قرفة, also pl. لفائف), a street/stair turn (عاللفة), or a wrench turn (لفة، لفتين).

examples.text: أكلت لفة قرفة سخنة مع الشاي.
examples.trans: I ate a warm cinnamon roll with tea.
Watch the tight turn on the stairs.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: ليمون.

examples.trans: The warm lemon cake is ready.
I squeezed half a lemon into the soup.

meanings.note: Negates verbs and في (ما بعرف 'I don't know', ما في 'there isn't'), and links conjunctions like قبل ما ('before') and بعد ما ('after').

examples.trans: Paper does not lose room names.
Have tea before you head out.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: مواسير.

examples.trans: The copper pipe started warming up right away.
Old pipes need maintenance in winter.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: مدراء.

examples.trans: She became the permanent front-desk manager at the guesthouse.
The manager welcomed the new guests.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: مرات.

examples.trans: The doorbell rang twice.
I read the letter three times.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: مطابخ.

examples.trans: The smell of bread is coming from the kitchen.
The guesthouse kitchen is spacious and clean.

meanings.note: Everyday preposition 'with'; takes pronoun suffixes to express 'have on one's person' (معي 'I have with me', معك حق 'you are right').

examples.trans: You are right, Nour!
Goodbye! (lit. go with safety)

meanings.note: Everyday preposition meaning 'from', 'of', or 'than' after comparatives.

examples.trans: I am Salma from the kitchen.
Breakfast is from seven-thirty to ten.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian numeral 'one hundred' (مية مرة 'a hundred times' — construct مية miyyet before a noun).

examples.trans: Yes, a hundred times yes!
I am one hundred percent sure.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بنسى, بينسى).

examples.trans: You forgot the notebook beside the soup bowl.
With all the rush, I completely forgot!

meanings.note: Clear, polite 'yes' (slightly warmer and more formal than casual آه).

examples.trans: Yes, room four is on the second floor!
Yes, a hundred times yes!

meanings.note: Signature Levantine word for 'now / right now' (pronounced halla' in Amman).

examples.trans: A taxi just stopped at the door now.
We will check the tag right now.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian/Levantine word for 'here' (لهون 'to here', من هون 'from here').

examples.trans: Here we use this big ledger.
Stay right here a minute.

meanings.note: Collective ورق ('paper / tree leaves'), singulative ورقة ('a sheet of paper / note'), plural أوراق ('documents / papers').

examples.trans: We use a paper ledger and a pencil.
He wrote a note on a small slip of paper.

meanings.note: Placed directly before a name or title when addressing someone in Arabic (يا نور 'Nour!', يا أستاذ 'sir!') and in exclamations (يا سلام! 'wonderful!').

examples.trans: Good morning, Tariq!
Oh, how lovely the sun is after the rain!

meanings.note: For door handles and bag handles, Jordanian speakers often say يد الباب / عاليد alongside إيد for the human hand.

examples.text: ارفعي يد الباب أول وبعدين ادفعي.
examples.trans: Lift the door handle first, then push.

examples.text: في بطاقة مربوطة على يد الشنتة.
examples.trans: There is a tag tied to the handle of the bag.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أيام.

examples.trans: Today the weather is sunny and warm in Amman.
Have a happy, successful day!

meanings.note: Appears in صباح النور ('morning of light', the standard reply to صباح الخير) and نور الشمس ('sunlight').

examples.trans: Good morning and welcome!
We read the card in the sunlight.
